author: NASASpaceflight
description:
Launch Window: September 2nd from 00:46 to 04:46 PDT (07:46-11:46 UTC)
Current T0: September 2nd at 01:18:09 PDT (08:18:09 UTC)

Mission: Falcon 9 launch of 27 Starlink v2 Mini satellites into orbit.
Launch location: Space Launch Complex 4E (SLC-4E), Vandenberg Space Force Base, Earth.
Target orbit: Low-Earth Orbit (LEO); 251x265km 70.01º
Booster: B1063-35; 28d 15h 13min 6s turnaround
Past customer missions: Sentinel 6 Michael Freilich, NASA's DART, Transporter-7, Iridium-9/OneWeb-19, SDA Tranche 0B, NROL-113, NROL-167, NROL-149, NAOS.
Past Starlink missions: v1.0-28, 4-11, 4-13, 3-1, 3-4, 4-31, 2-5, 5-13, 7-4, 7-7, 7-11, 7-17, 8-7, 9-3, 11-6, 11-7, 11-9, 11-22, 11-20, 11-23, 15-13, 17-25, 17-21, 17-28, 17-53.
Satellites launched: 979, will be 1006 after this mission
Booster recovery: Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY)
Fairing recovery: GO Beyond
Rocket trajectory: South-Southeast
Payload mass: Approximately 15.5 tonnes
Stats:
  - SpaceX's 715th launch overall.

title: SpaceX Launches Falcon 9 Starlink 15-23 from Vandenberg

author: NASASpaceflight
description:
SpaceX has announced plans for Starbase, Louisiana—a massive new Starship spaceport expected to feature at least 10 launch pads. The company hopes to begin construction in 2027, conduct its first launch in 2029, and eventually support an extraordinary Starship launch cadence.

Meanwhile, preparations for Starship Flight 14 are accelerating at Starbase, Texas. Booster 21 completed an approximately 15-second static fire involving all 33 Raptor engines, while Ship 41 has returned to the Production Site after completing its own static-fire campaign.

Also in this Starship Update:

• Ship 40 begins its journey home aboard the semi-submersible vessel Forte
• SpaceX targets a possible September launch for Flight 14
• Booster 21 completes its 33-engine static fire
• Ship 44 approaches completion inside Starfactory
• Pad 2 tests its hold-down clamps and Booster Quick Disconnects
• Starhopper celebrates the anniversary of its final 150-meter flight

title: Flight 14 Static Fires Complete! New Starbase Announced | Starship Update
